title: Expanded finite Q3 harmonic coarse-Schur stress
question: Does the exact two-block harmonic Schur assembly remain positive when the R-424 finite Q3 grid is enlarged to all R-419 cutoff-volume systems, with beta, orientation, alpha and tail threshold fixed?

new_perspective.principle: Treat the fixed-grid positivity of R-424 as a stress-test datum, not as uniformity. Re-run the same harmonic Schur and residual decomposition on the larger R-419 finite grid so any collapse or loss of eligible coverage is exposed before an analytic promotion is attempted.
route: Reuse the hash-pinned R-419 conditional Gibbs law, projected momentum conductance, R-421 tail transform and R-422 block-mean-zero split without retuning.
Use the exact R-406 harmonic Schur solve on every row with at least two core and two tail coordinates.
Recompute the residual gap through the R-422 block-mean-zero basis and compare it with the harmonic residual block.
Retain the conservative finite envelope 0.5*min(coarse Schur gap,residual gap); rows lacking two-by-two support remain reported but are not silently admitted.
Run a non-importing reversible-fixture lane, seven hostile mutations, the integrated verifier and a scalar Lean cross-check.
new_perspective.qft_bridge: The stress test only identifies whether finite positivity survives a declared enlargement. The unresolved QFT target remains a cutoff-, volume-, phase- and exhaustion-uniform common-core estimate followed by history and OS/KMS/GNS transfer.

finite_theorem.space: For each admitted conditional row, the sqrt(pi)-transformed graph is decomposed into the two block-constant span and its Euclidean orthogonal complement.
finite_theorem.harmonic_schur: The residual complement is eliminated by S=A_UU-A_UV A_VV^(-1) A_VU, with the Schur spectrum measured against the harmonic coarse mass.
finite_theorem.residual: The least eigenvalue of A_VV is recomputed independently on the block-mean-zero core and tail basis.
finite_theorem.combined_lower_envelope: The finite checked lower envelope is 0.5*min(coarse_gap,residual_gap).
finite_theorem.stress_interpretation: A positive envelope on this larger finite sample is a stress result only; it is not a bound uniform in any regulator or limit.

lean_crosscheck.boundary: Lean checks only the scalar envelope and finite-parameter bookkeeping; it does not formalize Gibbs rows, matrix eigensolvers, the grid stress, common cores or limits.

assumptions: The hash-pinned R-419 conditional law is positive and normalized and its projected momentum conductance is symmetric and nonnegative.
The beta grid, two orientations, alpha=1/40, tail threshold four and probability floor are fixed across every listed finite system.
The R-422 sqrt(pi) transform and block-mean-zero basis apply to disjoint core and tail supports with at least two coordinates each.
Every admitted residual block is positive, so the finite harmonic solve is defined.
Numerical comparisons use only the declared tolerances and never round a lower bound upward.
missing_assumptions: A cutoff-, volume-, phase- and exhaustion-uniform lower bound for the coarse Schur and residual forms on one Hamiltonian common core.
A common split-limit map and domain control as the regulator and volume vary.
Two-sided control of actual R-399 histories and transfer through the R-415 semigroup interface.
Hamiltonian-to-OS/KMS/GNS identification, physical-sector projection and a sectorwise coercive estimate.
promotion_criteria: Prove an analytic Schur/residual estimate on a domain-controlled unbounded Q3 common core.
Establish a positive envelope uniform in cutoff, volume, phase and exhaustion rather than only on this sample.
Transfer that envelope through the history and OS/KMS/GNS interfaces before any sector or physical promotion.
stop_conditions: A singular residual block, nonpositive Schur gap or residual disagreement stops the expanded-grid lane and is retained as a finite construction failure.
A collapse of the finite combined envelope is recorded without clipping and does not imply physical gaplessness.
Finite stress positivity cannot be promoted to a common-core, GNS, continuum, C6, Sector-A, Pre-A, Yang-Mills or mass-gap conclusion.
evidence_level: T0 / exact finite harmonic coarse-Schur decomposition on the expanded R-419 Q3 sample; no uniform theorem or physical conclusion
non_claims: No cutoff-, volume-, phase- or exhaustion-uniform coarse or residual bound.
No global Poincare theorem, common Hamiltonian core or common split-limit map.
No history transfer, OS/KMS/GNS reconstruction or sectorwise gap.
No continuum, C6, Sector-A, Pre-A, Yang-Mills or mass-gap conclusion.
boundary: R-425 is a finite expanded-grid stress test of the R-424 harmonic Schur assembly. It records support-eligibility boundaries and does not close the Q3LOCK parent gates.
next_unlock: Use the expanded-grid envelope only as a calibration target for an analytic common-core estimate; then test history transfer and OS/KMS/GNS identification.
no_overclaim: Positive finite envelopes on the expanded sample are matrix-level stress evidence, not regulator-independent or physical spectral gaps.
